description: Working with University College London and Camden Council, LDA Design, Norman Rourke Pryme and Darryl Moore have transformed Gordon Street, on the north side of Gordon Square in Bloomsbury to create a new 'college campus' for students, staff and the wider community. This has repurposed a road to create valuable new city green space. Find out what they did and how.

factsheet.heading: Changing Gordon Street
paragraphs: Directly outside the UCL Institute of Archaeology, Gordon Street in Bloomsbury was once used as a logistics yard and then road. Now, a pilot project for University College London (UCL) and Camden Council has reduced the space given over to cars and turned the street into a lively meeting place, a new campus for students and staff and the wider community to enjoy, and a great space for UCL to celebrate its bicentenary this year.

There is a flexible space for events, picnic tables, parking for 40 bikes, social nooks, drops kerbs to provide all-inclusive access and a variety of seating. Planting in raised planters along the street includes 67 trees, 5,000 perennials, grasses and ferns (140 species), planted in low-nutrient sand and crushed gravel to explore and experiment with resilient plant communities in a changing climate.

Join LDA Design director Cannon Ivers, project lead for the award-winning Strand in Westminster, and garden and landscape designer, Daryl Moore, to understand more about the changes made, what they mean for the community and the difference they are making.
